title: Exact row of two comaximal localizations
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and f,g comaximal elements. For any specified A-algebras S=A[1/f], T=A[1/g], P=A[1/(fg)] with their localization structures, the diagonal A to S x T is injective, its image is the kernel of the difference of the canonical maps S x T to P, and that difference is surjective. Zero rings and zero denominators are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00EJ; algebraization.tex Tag 0998, original proof step 3.

proof.text: If an element dies in both localizations, powers of f and g annihilate it. Coprimality of these powers and a Bezout identity imply it is zero.

source.place: Tag 00EJ; algebraization.tex Tag 0998, original proof step 3.

proof.text: For compatible fractions clear both denominators and then the power clearing their equality on the overlap. Increase both exponents to a common exponent E. If numerators a,b satisfy a*g^E=b*f^E, choose u*f^E+v*g^E=1; the numerator u*a+v*b realizes both fractions, by cancellation of the now invertible denominator powers.

source.place: Tag 00EJ; algebraization.tex Tag 0998, original proof step 3.

proof.text: Write an overlap fraction as z/(fg)^n. A Bezout identity u*f^n+v*g^n=1 shows that the pair v*z/f^n, -u*z/g^n maps to it. These arguments use Mathlib Away.exists_of_eq, Away.surj, IsCoprime.pow, and localization universal properties.

theorem localization_two_exact
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (f g : A) (hc : IsCoprime f g)
    (S T P : Type u) [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [CommRing P]
    [Algebra A S] [Algebra A T] [Algebra A P]
    [IsLocalization.Away f S] [IsLocalization.Away g T]
    [IsLocalization.Away (f * g) P] :
    let F := IsLocalization.Away.awayToAwayRight
      (S := S) (P := P) f g
    let G := IsLocalization.Away.awayToAwayLeft
      (S := T) (P := P) g f
    Function.Injective (fun x : A ↦
      (algebraMap A (S) x, algebraMap A (T) x)) ∧
    Function.Exact (fun x : A ↦
      (algebraMap A (S) x, algebraMap A (T) x))
      (fun x : S × T ↦ F x.1 - G x.2) ∧
    Function.Surjective
      (fun x : S × T ↦ F x.1 - G x.2)
